text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leftist leader Deniz Baykal claims Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan kept quiet despite the insulting statements of the Libyan president because Erbakan's Welfare Party was given $500,000 from Libya before general polls.
- Five deputies from the conservative wing of the government declared their support for oppositon motion to topple the government.
- President Suleyman Demirel rejects 200 government decrees.
- Investigation into Yuksekova incidents carried by out by Republican People's Party warns Turkey against civil war.
- Erbakan defends his visit to Libya saying that Tripoli was persuaded that separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) was a "terrorist" organisation.
- Italy supports Turkey becoming full member of the European Union.
- Democratic Left Party MP beats a traffic policewoman for stopping him after running a red traffic light.
- Opposition unites under a motion asking for Erbakan's resignation.
